newsitem.title: POLAND: BFK sees no payout for 1996, mulls '97.
newsitem.headline: BFK sees no payout for 1996, mulls '97.

text.p: Polish cable maker BFK will put 98.7 percent of last year's 24-million-zloty net profit into reserves and will consider making its first payout from 1997's profits, a representative of the firm's management board said.
"We were considering paying a dividend for the first time for 1996 but for the time being we want to invest a lot," Andrzej Szukala told Reuters on Friday.
Szukala said the firm's plan to invest about 35 million zlotys this year and 30 million next year to boost production would largely be financed by own funds and likely by loans as well.
On April 18 the firm's shareholders vote on the move which awards the rest of 1996 profits to a social fund for employees and to members of the supervisory board.
